BANCOMAT and CBI Sign an MOU to Build Italian Infrastructure Supporting the Digital Euro, With Nexi as Technology Partner
summary:
CBI, BANCOMAT and Nexi announce the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding for the launch of a strategic collaboration to build an Italian infrastructure supporting the digital euro, which will be developed with Nexi as technology partner. The solution will enable banks and Payment Service Providers (PSPs) to manage the processing of the digital euro, the issuance of which is subject to the ongoing legislative process, and connect to future Eurosystem services through a shared platform, with the objective of reducing investments and implementation costs, accelerating market entry, and streamlining technology upgrades.
The project aims to contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of the Italian financial system during a decisive phase for the evolution of European payments. The digital euro would complement cash as an additional form of money issued by the Central Bank and would be available to citizens, businesses, and public administrations within the euro area. 
The platform will be developed based on a shared, modular, and scalable infrastructure, in line with the European Central Bank’s roadmap and the evolution of the European regulatory framework. The goal is to foster adequate preparation among Italian operators and offer a coordinated response to a transformation set to impact the entire payments market.
The initiative combines the complementary expertise of the three organisations: CBI's experience in managing shared infrastructures and services for the financial sector; BANCOMAT's role as the national reference payment network; and Nexi’s established industrial and technological capabilities in digital payments across Europe.
Governance is entrusted to an equal partnership between CBI and BANCOMAT. Nexi will support the development of the solution as the technology partner, with contribution from TAS – an IT company specialised in payment solutions.
The infrastructure manages the connection of operators, the functions necessary for utilising the digital euro, and access to the central Eurosystem.
The model will be open, interoperable, and independent of individual technologies, with the aim of promoting service portability and accessibility even for smaller-sized operators.
For banks and PSPs, sharing the infrastructure will facilitate economies of scale, reducing costs, implementation risks, and the time required to offer new services. By streamlining activities, the shared platform can facilitate entry, especially for smaller operators, expanding competition and promoting the adoption of the digital euro.
“The digital euro marks a turning point for the European payment system. With this initiative, CBI is leveraging over thirty years of experience in building collaborative infrastructures to help banks and PSPs navigate change sustainably and effectively, in line with the path defined by the Eurosystem,” says Liliana Fratini Passi, Managing Director of CBI. “Italy can play a leading role. We want to combine skills, investments, and operational capabilities to equip the country with an open national platform capable of supporting the Italian market and contributing to the development of the digital euro in Europe.”
“The adoption of the digital euro will necessarily depend on the ability to involve those who operate daily on the ground, in direct contact with citizens and merchants, and to leverage already established payment networks and solutions,” states Fabrizio Burlando, CEO of BANCOMAT. “As systemic players, we have a duty to promote awareness of the new tool, favouring its integration into existing services and payment habits, and making its use simple. To this end, an effort is required from the entire payments sector so that the digital euro can become a practically utilised tool for citizens and businesses, enhancing its complementarity with solutions already present on the market.”
“The digital euro represents an important opportunity to strengthen the integration and competitiveness of the European payment system - says Bernardo Mingrone, CEO of Nexi Group - Nexi has always played a significant role in this journey, from the experiments promoted by the ECB to participation in the pilot, and up to network connectivity services: the collaboration with CBI and BANCOMAT constitutes a further contribution, putting our industrial and technological capabilities at the service of a shared solution that will facilitate the access of banks and financial operators to the future services of the digital euro.”
The MoU builds on established foundations, bringing together key players such as Intesa Sanpaolo together with isybank, the digital bank of the Group, which were among the first to join the project with BANCOMAT’s collaboration for technological aspects, as well as Nexi, which will use the platform for its direct merchants, and Poste Italiane, which, in addition to participating in the initiative, will make the Group’s cloud services available. The initiative, which is open to the entire banking and financial sector, has also attracted expressions of interest from a leading industry player, such as MPS. 
The platform has been designed with ambitions that go beyond national borders. It can be made accessible to European operators and integrated with other initiatives dedicated to digital currency and new payment instruments.
The collaboration between market infrastructures and technological enterprises thus offers Italy the opportunity to leverage its industrial expertise and contribute to building a more integrated and resilient European system.

content: BANCOMAT, CBI, and Nexi have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to build a shared Italian infrastructure supporting the digital euro. The initiative aims to help banks and Payment Service Providers manage digital euro processing and connect to future Eurosystem services, reducing implementation costs and fostering market competitiveness. The open, modular platform will involve key financial players and has ambitions to integrate with broader European payment systems.
content_ta: BANCOMAT, CBI மற்றும் Nexi நிறுவனங்கள் digital euro-வை ஆதரிக்கும் வகையில் இத்தாலிய உள்கட்டமைப்பை உருவாக்குவதற்கான புரிந்துணர்வு ஒப்பந்தத்தில் கையெழுத்திட்டுள்ளன. இந்த முயற்சியானது வங்கிகள் மற்றும் Payment Service Providers-க்கு digital euro செயலாக்கத்தை நிர்வகிக்கவும், எதிர்கால Eurosystem சேவைகளுடன் இணைக்கவும் உதவும். இதன் மூலம் செலவுகளைக் குறைத்து, சந்தைப் போட்டியை அதிகரிக்கச் செய்வதோடு, திறந்த மற்றும் மாடுலர் தளமாக இது செயல்படும்.

summary:
The post Bitcoin Flashes Buy Signal: Can BTC Rebound as $61K Support Holds? appeared first on Coinpedia Fintech News
Bitcoin is showing a potential reversal signal after its recent sharp sell-off, with a closely watched technical indicator now turning bullish on the three-day chart. The TD Sequential has flashed a buy signal, raising hopes that BTC could recover after falling toward key support levels. The signal comes as bearish momentum weighs on the market, …
content: Bitcoin is showing a potential reversal signal following a sharp market sell-off. A closely watched technical indicator, the TD Sequential, has turned bullish on the three-day chart. This development raises hopes that BTC could mount a recovery after falling toward key support levels near $61,000, even as broader bearish momentum continues to weigh on the cryptocurrency market.
